Article Title: ‘If match umpire is biased, what is the point of playing?’ Sachin Pilot questions CEC’s neutrality
Article Text:
Pilot questions CEC's neutrality

Pilot questions CEC appointment process, immunity law

Congress plans public impeachment proceeding against CEC

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sachin Pilot on Saturday questioned the neutrality of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that his conduct and the process governing his appointment and post-retirement immunity had raised concerns about the independence of the Election Commission.In an interview with news agency ANI, Pilot alleged that the CEC's actions had undermined public confidence in the electoral institution and called for accountability over the alleged deletion of names from electoral rolls.“If a match umpire is biased, what is the point of playing?”, Pilot said, questioning how voters could have faith in elections if the neutrality of the institution conducting them was under scrutiny.He referred to the alleged deletion of 13.3 crore names from electoral rolls, calling it a challenge to the fundamental right to vote. “13.3 crore people's names are known to be struck off the electoral rolls. It's a big challenge to what we believe is the most fundamental issue in our republic, which is the right to vote,” he said.Pilot claimed that the Congress had submitted documentary evidence of alleged wrongdoing by Gyanesh Kumar during his tenure as CEC.“There has been enough tangible data and documents proof given for the wrongdoings that Gyanesh Kumar has conducted through his term as Chief Election Commissioner,” he said.Pilot also questioned the legal provisions governing the appointment of the CEC and the immunity granted to the office-holder after demitting office.He said the earlier selection process involved the Prime Minister, the leader of opposition and the Chief Justice of India, and questioned the government's decision to change the composition of the selection panel.He also challenged the need for a law granting the CEC immunity after leaving office.“What was the need for the government to pass a new law which gives the chief election commissioner immunity for life? Now, he is the only person in the country, not the Prime Minister, not the chief ministers, not the Director of Intelligence or the Army Chief, but the only man who, after demitting office, will have immunity for life,” Pilot said.He alleged that the government had failed to address questions raised by the opposition in Parliament, arguing that the lack of answers had made it necessary to take the issue to the public.“As a political party, we are within our rights to raise this issue and demand answers,” he said.Pilot said the opposition was seeking to create awareness, particularly among young people, about the importance of independent electoral institutions. He maintained that institutions expected to function transparently should remain above political affiliations.He also said the legal challenge was already under way, with cases pending before the Supreme Court.“The fight is already going on at multiple levels. We also went to the Supreme Court. The cases are ongoing and are sub judice. The Election Commission has also given a clarification, which obviously you are not convinced about,” he said.The INDIA bloc has planned a public impeachment proceeding against CEC Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday. The event was postponed on Friday due to rain. The opposition bloc is also scheduled to hold a rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday against the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Congress leader Sachin Pilot questions neutrality of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. Pilot questions CEC appointment process, immunity law.Congress plans public impeachment proceeding against CEC on Saturday. Opposition bloc also scheduled to hold a rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday.

Article Title: Firecracker ban: No point in passing orders without enforcement, says SC
Article Text:
SC said it is not inclined to completely ban firecrackers but warned authorities that orders are meaningless without ground-level enforcement

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday said it was not inclined to completely ban firecrackers, but there was no point in passing orders and directions every year unless authorities implement them on the ground.“It concerns every living being,” a bench of Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale observed while hearing a matter on the bursting of firecrackers in Delhi-NCR.Additional solicitor-general Aishwarya Bhati told the bench about the measures taken by Delhi govt and Commission for Air Quality Management to deal with air pollution.“There is no point in passing orders and directions unless you give effect to them on the ground, otherwise, it becomes a mockery,” the bench observed, while stressing enforcement.While saying that it was not an adversarial matter, the bench observed that authorities have to take up the issue seriously and take action. “You have to really regulate it. Every year we are trying to balance it out but unless there is cooperation from everyone, it can’t be done,” it said.“We also understand the sentiments of the public. We are not inclined to completely ban, but don’t push us to take a very harsh stand,” the bench told Bhati.Bhati said a series of measures have been taken which would come into effect from Nov, including curbs on older vehicles, construction and demolition activity and staggered office timings in Delhi. “We are geared up to deal with the pollution season which unfortunately happens,” she said.Centre also told the bench that its internal consultation on the issue pertaining to the use of barium in firecrackers was going on. Bhati requested the bench to grant three weeks to complete the consultation.The top court was hearing two petitions, including a suo motu case concerning air pollution in NCR covering issues like firecrackers, stubble burning and solid waste management. The other plea relates to a ban on manufacturing firecrackers.During the hearing, an advocate, assisting the apex court as an amicus curiae in the suo motu case, said bursting firecrackers releases a huge amount of hazardous particulate matter (PM) which enters the human body and causes damage to lungs and other organs.She said during Dussehra last week, there was a spike in the Air Quality Index (AQI) in Delhi-NCR. Flagging the issue of enforcement, the amicus said there was no proper mechanism to assess whether the firecrackers which are being sold are actually green crackers.The bench had said that a middle ground would have to be found by specifying hours during which firecrackers could be used.
Article Summary: SC said it is not inclined to completely ban firecrackers but warned authorities that orders are meaningless without ground-level enforcement. “There is no point in passing orders and directions unless you give effect to them on the ground, otherwise, it becomes a mockery,” the bench observed, while stressing enforcement.

Article Title: 'No' to peace bond, 'yes' to INDIA bloc: Has Neha Bora outsmarted CJP leaders?
Article Text:
AISA president Neha Bora and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke

Neha Bora on why she would not sign peace bond

Neha Bora, along with Lok Sabha leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi, during the opposition's protest.

NEW DELHI: When Neha Bora recently said “AISA will not be a part of normalising the signing of peace bonds”, she inadvertently highlighted a contrast that the Jantar Mantar 2.0 protests against SIR and "vote chori" had brought to the fore. Neha’s refusal to sign the peace bond before a special executive magistrate and her subsequent challenge to the police move drew an obvious parallel. Did the CJP leaders - Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Sourav Das - give in to peace bond pressure easily?“Peace bonds are being weaponised to curb democratic protests. Signing such peace bonds is no less than signing away our democratic right to dissent,” the AISA national president said and claimed that she was detained within 10 minutes of protesting at Mandi House on October 16 and was told that she and other protesters were in breach of peace.“On one side, the Constitution gives us the right to dissent. On the other hand, such peace bonds are invoked only to detain people in the name of breach of peace. Therefore, signing such peace bonds is a principally wrong decision for us. It is no less than signing away our democratic right to dissent,” Bora said defending her decision.Bora has still not signed the bond and is awaiting copies of 6 FIRs cited as her criminal antecedents in peace-bond proceedings.This, after she insisted for all documents relied upon in the show-cause notice seeking execution of her peace bond.Now, let’s rewind to October 10.The CJP’s call for Jantar Mantar 2.0 on October 10 had, as expected, evoked great national interest and anticipation. All eyes were on Abhijeet Dipke and his associates Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who had in June-July this year led a successful youth mobilisation against NEET paper leak. The CJP-led protests had ensured that Dharmendra Pradhan was forced to resign as Union education minister. After all, they were the new heroes of GenZ, who had left the politicians far behind.But ahead of October 10, the national capital saw an unprecedented clampdown. The Delhi Police closed down anything and everything that could facilitate the movement of protesters to Jantar Mantar. For the CJP leadership, the message was loud and clear - they will not get a free passage, unlike in June when they were allowed to gather and mobilise youth at Jantar Mantar for their protests against NEET paper leak.But October 10 morning started with an anticlimax. The top 3 CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das travelled together from Mumbai to Delhi and were detained from aircraft as soon as they landed in the national capital. Thousands of protesters who had responded to their calls, braved the police clampdown. They were all detained.The CJP leaders were released a day later after giving an undertaking to maintain public order. Delhi Police said a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was furnished for CJP activists Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das for maintaining peace and good behaviour for one year, following their preventive arrest on October 10.The CJP leaders made two more attempts to reclaim the streets - when Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka tried to reach Jantar Mantar and again when Dipke urged people to join the "Lehra Do Tiranga" march with the national flag at Central Park in Connaught Place.However, they were detained again and made to sign peace bonds to come out of detention. And while the CJP leaders failed to recreate the magic of Jantar Mantar 1.0, AISA leader Neha Bora took the centrestage. The AISA national president was detained 5 times between October 2 and October 11. However, every time she was released, she would come back to the streets and continue with her protests.During the peak of the protests, Neha Bora hogged the headlines for foxing the police. On October 11, Neha Bora announced a gathering at RK Ashram Marg Metro Station around 2:30pm as part of demonstrations heading toward central Delhi and Jantar Mantar.Heavy police deployment and barricades were set up around RK Ashram Marg to prevent demonstrators from moving toward Jantar Mantar. During the confrontation, police mistakenly chased and detained another protester whose face was partially covered, believing her to be Neha Bora.While police attention was focused at RK Ashram Marg, Neha Bora surfaced near Connaught Place (CP), breaching barricades and running alongside fellow demonstrators in a dash that went viral on social media.Little wonder then, when a user on X called Neha Bora "more talented" than CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and described her as a "complete GenZ icon", Dipke responded simply: "I agree." The X user had posted: "Maturity is realizing Neha Bora is more talented than Abhijeet Dipke. A complete GenZ icon with an absolutely ridiculous aura.” It was a comparison that manifested all along the “vote chori” protests.Neha Bora was on the streets every time she was released from detention by the police. She was everywhere - with the CJP leadership, the social activists and also the politicians. When Rahul Gandhi chose to walk behind her during one of the protest marches of INDIA bloc, it spoke volumes about the impact she had made with her street politics. Clearly, the campaign against “vote chori” had put the spotlight on Neha Bora, even as the CJP struggled to find their way to the centre stage of the protests.For the CJP, it was a harsh realisation that a lot had changed between July and October. Unlike the anti-NEET paper leak protests in June-July, the Congress-led INDIA bloc this time around were already on the streets demanding resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Interestingly, while the INDIA bloc’s original protest schedule had only one announced street protest on October 6, the group returned back to the streets four days in a row till October 9, which was a day before the announced CJP protest.The CJP and the Congress had stayed away from each other during the anti-NEET protests. After Jantar Mantar 1.0 was over, the 'cockroaches' carried out their own campaigns in different states, while the Congress shifted focus to protests against SIR and CEC Gyanesh Kumar.Abhijeet Dipke has announced that he has no political plans and would prefer to keep CJP as a pressure group. So when CJP announced support for INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally, it set tongues wagging about their political ambitions.With CJP’s Jantar Mantar 2.0 not shaping out as they would have hoped, perhaps its leadership should take a leaf out of Saurav Das’s advice on X to a Congress “soldier” who had questioned why youth Congress and NSUI activists were being detained as soon as they hit the streets and cockroaches were allowed to roam free. Responding to him, CJP co-founder Saurav Das had then said: “if u guys r detained immediately, then u must rethink ur strategy. don’t blame others for ur failures.”The context of that remark was different and CJP’s Jantar Mantar 2.0 campaign was in no way a failure, but Sourav's take on “rethinking strategy” perhaps holds true for the cockroaches at present.
Article Summary: Neha Bora's refusal to sign peace bond drew an obvious parallel with the Jantar Mantar 2.0 protests against SIR and "vote chori" The AISA national president was detained 5 times between October 2 and October 11. She has still not signed the bond and is awaiting copies of 6 FIRs cited as her criminal antecedents.

Article Title: Discourage weaponisation of rape law in relationships gone sour: SC
Article Text:
Supreme Court warns against misuse of rape laws after consensual relationships turn sour, saying breakups cannot retrospectively criminalise consensual sex

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Society and courts must discourage weaponisation of criminal law against men in the aftermath of an emotional discord and breakup of a consenting romantic relationship, Supreme Court said Friday, expressing concern over the disturbing trend of criminal provision of rape being invoked to prosecute men after relationship turns sour.A bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan said the legislature never intended consensual sexual acts between adults to be retrospectively criminalised merely because the relationship came to an end. "It is unfortunate that despite judicial deprecation, this trend is increasing, and it is a matter of concern as often settlement of disputes come with huge monetary considerations to be borne by the male accused," it said.The court underlined "a worrying trend in recent years, wherein consensual relationship is given a colour of sexual assault"."In fact, such an approach denudes the man of any agency entirely, as the mere factum of being in a consensual relationship at one point would bind him to it entirely for fear of being accused of rape at a subsequent point of time," SC said, while allowing the plea of a man who was being prosecuted for rape on a complaint filed by his erstwhile live-in partner with whom he shared a relationship for seven years..The top court also cautioned that the trend carries the risk of undermining the gravity of the serious criminal offence of rape.
Article Summary: Supreme Court expresses concern over disturbing trend of criminal provision of rape being invoked to prosecute men after relationship turns sour. Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan said legislature never intended consensual sexual acts between adults to be retrospectively criminalised.

Article Title: MLC election results: BJP wins big, but Congress and Samajwadi Party send a message from Nagpur, Varanasi
Article Text:
BJP's big win in MLC elections comes with setbacks in Nagpur and Varanasi

BJP-led NDA secured 16 of the 28 MLC seats across four states, while the SP won five seats in Uttar Pradesh and Congress retained Nagpur in Maharashtra.

BJP mocks Congress over 'zero' seats

BJP president Nitin Nabin targeted Congress over its poor performance in the MLC elections, pointing out that voting had taken place using ballot papers.

Nagpur win gives Congress a chance to respond

Congress leader Jairam Ramesh questioned the BJP's setbacks in Nagpur and Varanasi after PM Modi mocked the party's performance in the MLC elections.

Varanasi setback gives SP a boost ahead of 2027

What do the results mean for 2027?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The MLC elections across four states brought both shock and cheer for the BJP and Congress. While the Congress suffered a humiliating defeat in Karnataka, where it is in power but failed to win a single seat, the BJP faltered in two constituencies which mattered the most. One being Nagpur, which is home to the RSS headquarters, and Varanasi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency.The BJP nevertheless emerged as the largest party, winning 13 of the 28 seats contested, while its allies took the NDA's tally to 16. The alliance swept all four seats in Karnataka, won six of the 11 seats in Uttar Pradesh and secured four of the eight seats in Bihar. In Maharashtra, the ruling Mahayuti won two of the five seats, while the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi secured three.The Congress's only victory came from Nagpur, a political stronghold of Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and Union minister Nitin Gadkari. In Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party retained the Varanasi Teachers' constituency and was heading towards victory in the Graduates' seat, both of which it had won in 2020.What began as celebrations and sharp jibes at the Congress on Wednesday turned into a war of words on Thursday, as the results in Nagpur and Varanasi gave the opposition grounds to question the BJP's claims of electoral dominance.As the early results came in on Wednesday, BJP leaders targeted the Congress over its poor performance, particularly in Karnataka, where the party is in power but failed to win a single seat.PM Modi took a swipe at the opposition party on X, pointing out that voting in the four states had taken place using ballot papers."Guess how many seats Congress won?" he asked.The remark came amid the Congress's repeated allegations over electronic voting machines and its demand for a return to ballot-paper voting.BJP president Nitin Nabin also targeted the Congress, saying the party had failed to win public support despite voting being conducted using ballot papers."The people are repeatedly rejecting Congress' anarchist politics," Nabin said, adding that public trust remained with PM Modi irrespective of whether elections were conducted using EVMs or ballot papers.BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi also attacked Rahul Gandhi over his allegations of vote theft"Kamchori ki aadat chhodiye. Vote chori ka shabd apke muh se khud chhoot jayega," he said, asking the Congress leader to give up what he described as a habit of avoiding hard work.Congress candidate and sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJP's Sudhakar Kohale to retain the Nagpur Division Graduates' constituency after more than 40 hours of counting.Kohale had initially taken the lead before Wanjari overtook him through preferential votes.Nagpur is important for the BJP. Besides housing the RSS headquarters, it is associated with Fadnavis and Gadkari, both of whom campaigned for Kohale.The Congress had wrested the seat from the BJP in 2020, when Wanjari defeated Sandip Joshi. By retaining it in 2026, the party prevented the BJP from reclaiming a constituency it had dominated for decades.The Maharashtra Congress also targeted Fadnavis over a social media post in which he had claimed that the party had failed to win a single seat.Sharing a screenshot of what it said was a deleted post by Fadnavis, the party accused him of celebrating before counting was complete. The post had described the Congress's performance as a "big fat zero".The Congress said Fadnavis had been forced to delete the post after the Nagpur result and warned that the outcome was only a trailer of future political battles.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh also responded to PM Modi's remarks, questioning the BJP's losses in Nagpur and Varanasi."The Prime Minister needs to introspect, but instead, he's lecturing others! Before counting Congress's seats, I wish he'd also reflect on why the BJP lost both seats in his own parliamentary constituency of Varanasi, and how Congress managed to defeat the BJP in RSS's stronghold of Nagpur?" Ramesh said."Mr. Modi, stop the trolling," he added, accusing the government of failing to address inflation, unemployment and weak private investment.Ramesh claimed that voters in Varanasi, Nagpur, Lucknow, Prayagraj and Patna had expressed dissatisfaction with the Centre's policies.The BJP's biggest setback in Uttar Pradesh came from Varanasi, where the Samajwadi Party retained the Teachers' seat and established an unassailable lead in the Graduates' constituency.The BJP retained six of the 11 seats contested in the state, while the SP won four and was heading towards a fifth.The SP had won both Varanasi seats in 2020 as well. Six years later, the BJP has failed to dislodge the party from either constituency despite its strong presence in the region.Although the two MLC constituencies cover a wider geographical area than PM Modi's Lok Sabha seat, the results carry political significance given Varanasi's association with the Prime Minister since 2014.They also come after PM Modi's victory margin in Varanasi declined from nearly 4.8 lakh votes in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections to around 1.5 lakh in 2024.Across Uttar Pradesh, the SP's tally is set to rise from three seats in 2020 to five, while the BJP has retained its tally of six.The SP had also emerged as the largest party in Uttar Pradesh in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, winning 37 of the state's 80 parliamentary seats against the BJP's 33.BJP deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya acknowledged that the party had expected a better performance."These elections are decided by highly educated and qualified voters. The BJP has repeated its previous performance, but we expected to win more seats. We will examine why we fell short," Maurya said.The SP, meanwhile, has repeatedly accused the BJP of electoral irregularities, allegations the ruling party has rejected.On polling day, Akhilesh Yadav had claimed that the BJP was attempting to influence even the MLC elections, which have a limited electorate."If the BJP can do this in MLC polls for teachers and graduate constituencies where a limited number of people cast votes, one can imagine their preparation for the assembly polls," he had said.The NDA's overall tally shows that the BJP and its allies remain ahead in these Legislative Council contests. But the results in Nagpur and Varanasi also show that the party has struggled to regain certain seats despite its strong presence in both regions.In Uttar Pradesh, the SP and Congress are preparing to contest the 2027 assembly elections together, hoping to build on their performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls.The alliance won 43 of the state's 80 parliamentary seats in 2024, reducing the BJP's tally from 62 in 2019 to 33. Akhilesh Yadav has said the alliance will continue in 2027, although the two parties still need to settle their seat-sharing arrangement.The MLC results, however, cannot be treated as an indication of how the state will vote in the assembly elections. These contests involve a limited electorate of registered graduates and teachers, unlike assembly polls, which are decided by a much wider voter base.For the BJP, which is seeking a third consecutive term in Uttar Pradesh, the challenge will be to counter the opposition's gains. For the SP-Congress alliance, the question is whether it can repeat its 2024 Lok Sabha performance when the state's 403 assembly seats go to the polls in 2027.
Article Summary: BJP-led NDA secured 16 of the 28 MLC seats across four states, while the SP won five seats in Uttar Pradesh and Congress retained Nagpur in Maharashtra. PM Modi mocked Congress over its poor performance, pointing out that voting had taken place using ballot papers.

Article Title: Uttarakhand chopper flying: A lot has changed for better, but a lot remains to be done
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Hours after seven people on board an Aryan Aviation chopper died when it crashed near Gaurikund on June 15, 2025, the aviation ministry had found two helicopters of Trans Bharat — whose chopper crashed on Friday — were airborne “under unsuitable weather conditions. ” It had suspended the licences of both Trans Bharat pilots for six months.While the cause of Trans Bharat’s Friday crash in which six people lost their lives will be known once the inquiry report is out, there have been red flags regarding this and several other chopper operators in the hill region. The Uttarakhand govt has grounded Trans Bharat fleet for now.Aviation industry insiders point out that six days before Friday crash, another Trans Bharat helicopter carrying five pilgrims from Sahastradhara to Kedarnath via Guptkashi had made an emergency landing at Baurari stadium on Oct 24 “where children were playing.” Luckily all six, five passengers and the pilot, were safe that day and the chopper took off soon again.“On May 20, 2026, a Trans Bharat Bell 407 flying from Badrinath to Dehradun with seven people on board ran into severe downdrafts over the Chamba–Arakot sector of Tehri Garhwal. During the emergency landing that followed, its tail struck a 33 kV high-tension line. The pilot, a former IAF pilot, got everyone down uninjured,” said sources.Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) is probing this case.The Char Dham corridor has no single agency answerable for safety. While the DGCA licenses the operators and pilots, UCADA runs the helipads, sets slots and manages shuttle operations. The Sanjay Kumar Jha-headed parliamentary standing committee on transport, tourism and culture had in Aug 2025 called this arrangement “inherently unsafe and unsustainable.” It said there was a “responsibility vacuum” between the two agencies. It found that the DGCA was acting as a passive licensing authority. It also noted that India still has no mandatory, terrain-specific mountain-flying training or certification for pilots operating in the Himalaya.This changed significantly after last summer following a spate of chopper crashes in Uttarakhand. Air traffic control units are being set up, with Kedarnath having one now and Badrinath to get a unti soon. Routes have been defined in the region and take offs are both restricted in number and controlled in a defined pattern with some gap. This is a far cry from the almost unregulated chopper movement in the hill region till last summer.“System wise there has been a lot of improvement. The Char Dham Operations are quite extensive in every aspect. From commercial to maintenance and from operations to ATC, every department is working very hard to ensure safety and efficiency is achieved. After the season of 2025 , there are many different measures that are implemented to ensure highest safety standards are met. These include ATC at Sahastradhara and Sitapur to ensure that flying is well coordinated and controlled,” said Captain Nitin Welde, a senior chopper pilot who operates in Uttarakhand.“There’s a fuel bowser at Sahastradhara to ensure that IOCL supplies fuel in best possible manner. Take off and landing tarmac is separated from parking Tarmac to ensure orderly flow of positioning. There are CCTV cameras all across valley which give feed through a mobile app. All can get a live feed as regards weather valley. For higher helipads above 10,000 feet, the weight limitations are in place and that ensures higher reserve of power while landing and take off. Training for pilots has increased since last year. And there is adequate training in Char Dham sector as well as Kedar shuttles. The DGCA FOIs have been visiting the valley on a weekly basis and UCADA ops department is fully involved in a minute to minute monitoring and support,” added Captain Welde.“Friday was a sad day where it appears that weather in exit phase of Badri valley wasn’t good,” Captain Welde said.
Article Summary: The cause of Trans Bharat’s Friday crash in which six people lost their lives will be known once the inquiry report is out. There have been red flags regarding this and several other chopper operators in the hill region. The Uttarakhand govt has grounded Trans Bharats fleet for now.

Article Title: VHP questions timing of INDIA bloc rally amid Diwali, recalls Rahul Gandhi’s Bharat Jodo Yatra break
Article Text:
VHP on INDIA bloc rally

NEW DELHI: The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) on Saturday questioned the INDIA bloc’s decision to hold a rally on November 1 amid Diwali festivities, saying political parties should not ignore festivals, social harmony and the country’s economy in the name of politics.VHP national spokesperson Vinod Bansal pointed to a nine-day break during Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s Bharat Jodo Yatra, from December 25, 2022, to January 2, 2023, for Christmas and New Year celebrations. He questioned why the Opposition had not considered similar appeals to postpone its November 1 rally.In a post on X, Bansal said traders’ organisations in Delhi and members of the Hindu community had repeatedly urged the INDIA bloc to cancel or defer the rally, citing the possibility of disruptions to Diwali celebrations and losses to businesses dependent on the festival. He alleged that their appeals had been ignored.The remarks came ahead of the INDIA bloc’s planned rally at Ramlila Maidan over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls, with the Opposition demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The programme, initially scheduled for Friday, was postponed to Saturday due to rain in the national capital.The bloc has also announced a “public impeachment” of the CEC.Taking aim at it, the VHP spokesperson asked whether the leader of opposition and other political parties would fulfil their democratic responsibilities instead of engaging in what he called “mock politics” through mock impeachments and mock parliaments.
Article Summary: VHP national spokesperson Vinod Bansal pointed to a nine-day break during Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s Bharat Jodo Yatra for Christmas and New Year celebrations. He questioned why the Opposition had not considered similar appeals to postpone its November 1 rally. The remarks came ahead of the INDIA bloc's planned rally at Ramlila Maidan over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls.

Rahul Gandhi shared image on X

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday shared a heartfelt message remembering his grandmother and former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her 42nd death anniversary, recalling childhood moments spent with her and sharing a photograph from their time together.In a post on X, Rahul recalled sitting on her lap, holding her hands and repeating Sanskrit verses after her. Article Title: PM Modi attends ‘Anand Math’ play ahead of Ekta Diwas celebrations in Gujarat
Article Text:

EKTA NAGAR, KEVADIA: Anand Math, the literary source of ‘ Vande Mataram ’, was adapted into a grand, multimedia-based play and showcased at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, here on Friday in the presence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the eve of the Ekta Diwas, Sardar Patel’s birth anniversary.Sardar Patel’s birth anniversary on Oct 31 this year is focused on celebrating the end of armed Naxalism and 150 years of ‘Vande Mataram’. The prime minister is the chief guest at the Ekta Diwas events this year, organised here with the 'Statue of Unity’ as a backdrop. The one-and-a-half hour long play ‘Anand Math’ is directed by NSD, It is based on the abiding philosophy of Anand Math: that every person of India has a responsibility of building a bright future for the country and being aware of its cultural heritage.Members of Anand Math author Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay’ family sat beside the Prime minister, watching the dramatic recreation of the Bengali novel. The innovative use of digital screens to lend a cinematic edge to the sets, set the performance apart."The Chattopadhyay family is glad that Vande Mataram is being sung in full. Justice was not being done to the sentiment behind Anand Math when just two stanzas were sung," Shantanu Chatterjee, a member of the family who watched the play Anand Math, told TOI.The play, in fact, ended with the rendition of Vande Mataram in full.Ekta Nagar, which houses the towering statue of Sardar Patel and other tourist attractions, is the venue of Rashtriya Ekta Diwas Parade, which is almost on the lines of Republic Day parade in Delhi, possibly grander with several events organised alongside the parade. The town is currently glowing with festive lights, with lit up pieces of art showcasing the culture and traditions of each state. Tourists from all over the country have descended here to watch the 'Unity Day' spectacle.On Saturday, 7,000 people from 126 districts that at some point of time were affected by Left-wing extremism, will participate both as performers and spectators in the event.Around 2,000 artists drawn from the 126 districts will join the celebrations by putting up a drama performance, also directed by the National School of Drama (NSD), through which they will recount how their life and property were threatened when Naxalism was rampant in their area.In addition, around 5,000 local people from these 126 districts have been invited. They will not only be spectators for all the performances but will also, through their interactions, share the hardships they had to undergo at the hands of Maoists and how their lives have changed now.“Their participation will underline the resilience of communities that have endured conflict and highlight the role of cultural expression in strengthening national integration,” said Govind Mohan.The 2026 edition of the parade will also feature march-past by contingents of all the central armed police forces (CAPFs) and state police personnel who were in the forefront of the decisive fight against left-wing extremist violence. A short film will play on LED screens at the venue as the contingents pass in front of the Prime Minister, the chief guest, summarising the salient feature of their achievements in eliminating armed Naxalism.The Ekta Diwas parade, to be held in the evening hours this year, will also feature tableaux designed around the theme of “Vande Mataram” and constructed by the people and private entities with corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds, with no involvement of the govt. The 15 designs for the tableaux, selected through competition, are based on the implications of ‘Vande Mataram’ on nationhood and development.There will also be a cultural programme curated entirely by people from different states and communities who have made Gujarat their home. Around 5,000 artists will showcase dances and culture of their respective states through this mega-performance.
Article Summary: Anand Math, the literary source of ‘ Vande Mataram ’, was adapted into a grand, multimedia-based play and showcased at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the chief guest at the Ekta Diwas events this year, organised here with the 'Statue of Unity' as a backdrop.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Preliminary results from one tracking group show 85% of students closed their foundational skills gaps.Oakland Unified is adding $25 million of its own for small-group tutoring. The district aims to serve up to 4,500 students a year by 2029.Curry has put his name behind the foundation since 2019, and the totals are big. Over seven years, it has invested more than $100 million in Oakland kids, delivered 35 million meals, remodeled 25 schoolyards and six gymnasiums, and redesigned 14 cafeterias. More than 1 million new books have reached OUSD students.For the four-time champion, learning has a clear target: every Oakland elementary student reading proficiently by the end of third grade. The foundation says its high-impact tutoring now reaches more than 10,000 OUSD students.July brought two honors. The Hollywood Reporter named the Currys Philanthropists of the Year, and Curry received the Muhammad Ali Sports Humanitarian Award.Books go home with kids, too. Last December’s book fairs ran at 47 OUSD schools, where more than 17,000 students could each choose four new books to take home. The plan called for more than 68,000 books in all.Fundraising comes from several directions. An April sneaker auction of more than 70 pairs worn by Curry raised $1.7 million, and the Workday Charity Classic added $5.6 million, helped by a matching gift from Workday CEO Aneel Bhusri.
Article Summary: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have committed $25 million over five years to give 10,000 Oakland elementary students one-on-one reading tutoring. The Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation announced the plan on Aug. 29, 2024. It is the largest literacy investment the foundation has made.

Article Title: Patrick Stewart's wife wanted Lionel Messi, not Cristiano Ronaldo, and the actor made sure her wish came true
Article Text:

Patrick Stewart went out of his way to introduce his wife to Lionel Messi

Messi's reaction made the meeting even more special

Patrick Stewart had two football icons in front of him at the 2017 Best FIFA Football Awards in London. Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi were both among the guests, but the actor had a different priority. He wanted to make his wife, Sunny Ozell, happy by introducing her to Messi. The encounter required some effort, as Stewart had to get past security to reach the Argentine. His story has resurfaced following his death at 86, offering a glimpse of the personal side of the actor beyond his celebrated screen roles.Stewart attended the 2017 awards ceremony with Ozell, who had developed a strong admiration for Messi. Her interest in football had grown after watching the Argentine play, and the actor knew that meeting him would mean a great deal to her.He had even promised to make the introduction if Messi attended the event. Stewart recalled the conversation during an interview with the SAG-AFTRA Foundation.“I knew he was going to be at that event, and I told my wife: ‘If he’s there, I’ll do everything in my power to put the two of you face to face.’ She told me, ‘And what happens if he becomes my ‘hall pass’?’ I answered: ‘That’s fine by me,'” Stewart said.Keeping that promise was not easy. The actor recalled seeing Messi, Ronaldo and Argentine legend Diego Maradona at the ceremony, but security made it difficult to approach them.“It was really difficult because there was security as you’ve never seen. Messi was there, Cristiano Ronaldo, and the other great Argentine… Diego Maradona, the Hand of God. I crashed into the security door. ‘Excuse me, excuse me,’ I said. ‘I’m Patrick Stewart,’ I embarrassed myself.”The actor eventually managed to get close to Messi, although finding him in the crowd proved another challenge.Stewart said Messi had turned around and leaned over his seat, making it difficult to spot him among the other guests. When the footballer finally sat up, the two came face to face.“I stood behind him, and he sat up, turned, and we were face to face. And you’ll see, his face… this is very moving for me… It simply lit up before me. And I said to him: ‘Mr. Messi, please, my wife…'” Stewart recalled.Ozell got the photograph she had hoped for. Stewart took a picture of his wife standing beside Messi rather than asking for a selfie. The moment also brought an unexpected gesture from Messi's wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, who asked for a photograph with the actor.“There they shook hands. And I said to them: ‘Please, can I take a photo of you together?’ So I took their photo; it wasn’t a selfie. I took the photo of my wife with Messi, side by side, and then his wife (Antonela Roccuzzo) said: ‘And I want a photo with you!'”Ozell later explained just how much the meeting meant to her. She had met many famous people during her years working in New York restaurants, but Messi was different.“After having worked in fancy New York restaurants for years, I met a lot of important people and became quite immune to nerves. And, to be honest, there aren’t many living human beings in the world I would love to meet. But Messi? Lionel Messi? You can bet your sweet ass I was scared.”Stewart also shared a selfie with Messi on social media, adding a short but memorable caption: “I met a God tonight!”What makes the story stand out is that Stewart was not trying to make his own celebrity encounter the focus. He had made a promise to his wife and wanted to keep it. The fact that Messi's family also joined the moment made the evening even more memorable.
Article Summary: Patrick Stewart met Lionel Messi at the 2017 Best FIFA Football Awards. The actor had promised his wife, Sunny Ozell, that he would introduce her to the Argentine. Messi's wife Antonela Roccuzzo also asked for a photo with the actor.

Article Title: "They put a bird's eye view of where we live": Kylie Kelce has a blunt response for critics questioning her family's decision to own multiple neighboring homes

How do the Thunder cope without three starters?

Oklahoma City has lost a third starter to a significant injury in a single week. Chet Holmgren will miss eight to 10 weeks with a small tear in the patellar tendon of his right knee, the Thunder announced Friday night. The center had a procedure that day to avoid surgery, and the timeline points to a return in early 2027. Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace went down last Sunday and have both had operations since. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander now heads into November with a thinner lineup around him and a lot more to carry.Holmgren saw several specialists after feeling mild discomfort last Sunday. By Friday the team decided to “perform a biological treatment today to address a small patellar tendon tear,” according to its statement. The team called the procedure successful.A league source told NBC Sports the treatment is likely platelet-rich plasma therapy, a common option across pro sports that spares a player the more invasive repair. Eight to 10 weeks puts the 7-footer back on the floor in the first couple of weeks of 2027.He was averaging 12.0 points and 9.3 rebounds this season. Last season he put up 17.1 points, 8.9 rebounds and 1.9 blocks, and earned first-team All-Defensive and third-team All-NBA honors.Injuries have followed Holmgren since the Thunder took him No. 2 in the 2022 draft. A broken foot wiped out the 2022-23 season, and a fractured pelvis cost him a few months of 2024-25 before he returned for the title run. This is the third major one.Williams has a fractured fibula and a dislocated left ankle after an ugly fall against the Clippers. Wallace tore the labrum in his left shoulder in the same game. Wallace had surgery Friday and Williams on Wednesday, and both will be re-evaluated before the regular season ends. All three starters are key defenders.The roster was already lighter. Offseason trades sent Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe away for financial reasons, and Oklahoma City signed Ochai Agbaji on Friday for wing help.Isaiah Hartenstein, rookie Aday Mara and Jaylin Williams will soak up frontcourt minutes, and Kenrich Williams may move into the starting five. Gilgeous-Alexander, the back-to-back MVP, will carry most of the scoring load with Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain beside him.

In a statement shared with People in May 2021, the four-time Grand Slam champion recalled watching Tamaki work hard to support her passion for tennis.“Growing up, I saw my mother work incredibly hard to support me and my passion for play,” Naomi said. She helped support the family financially while Naomi and Mari trained and competed. The costs of developing two young tennis players included equipment, court access and travel. Tamaki took on long working hours to help meet those demands. Naomi later spoke about seeing her mother push through exhaustion, an image that stayed with her as she grew older.There was also a personal side to Tamaki’s support. Naomi grew up in a Japanese-Haitian household, with her mother helping her stay connected to her Japanese roots. The family eventually chose to have Naomi represent Japan, even though she grew up in the United States.For Naomi, her mother’s influence was not limited to tennis. Tamaki encouraged her to accept her background and feel comfortable with her identity. That support became part of the foundation behind the player fans know today.While Tamaki helped make the tennis journey possible, Leonard François took responsibility for teaching his daughters the game. His decision came after watching Venus and Serena Williams compete at the 1999 French Open.Leonard saw similarities between the Williams sisters and his own daughters. He also studied how their father, Richard Williams, had guided their careers. Although Leonard had little tennis experience, he began learning the sport through instructional books and videos before coaching Naomi and Mari.“The blueprint was already there. Leonard then put both girls through demanding practice sessions, with thousands of balls hit as they worked on their game. Naomi wrote that she loved her father and felt grateful for everything she learned from him, both on and off the court.Tamaki’s hard work helped provide the opportunity. Leonard’s decision to teach himself tennis gave Naomi and Mari their first lessons. Their approaches were different, but both parents helped build the path that Naomi would eventually take to the top of the sport.

Article Title: Josh Allen's massive Bills contract vs Lamar Jackson's Ravens deal: Inside the money behind their NFL stardom
Article Text:
Josh Allen vs Lamar Jackson contract details (Getty Images)

Josh Allen's Bills contract versus Lamar Jackson's Ravens deal

Lamar Jackson's cap hit is Baltimore's problem

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Josh Allen has $250 million in guaranteed money. Lamar Jackson has $185 million and no new contract. Allen's six-year, $330 million extension with the Bills runs through 2030, while Jackson's five-year, $260 million deal with the Ravens expires after 2027. Allen signed in March 2025, Jackson in April 2023. Both are former MVPs, and both are paid like it. Allen's guarantee alone beats Jackson's by $65 million. Buffalo has its quarterback signed three seasons longer than Baltimore has Jackson. The Ravens, meanwhile, face a cap spike and an unfinished negotiation.Josh Allen's contract is the newer and larger of the two. The Bills gave him a six-year, $330 million extension, with $250 million guaranteed, in March 2025, after his MVP season. The deal averages $55 million a year. At the time, that lifted him from 14th among quarterbacks in average annual value to a tie for second.Jackson's deal came first, and it was built differently. He agreed to five years and $260 million, a $52 million average that was the highest in the league then. The contract carried a $72.5 million signing bonus and $185 million in guarantees. But only $135 million was fully guaranteed at signing.That figure rose to $156 million after one season and reached $185 million after two.Allen's guarantee is $65 million bigger, and it sits on a contract that runs three years longer. Jackson represents himself and has never had an agent.Allen's signing bonus was $56.7 million, smaller than the $72.5 million Jackson received. His cap hit is still heavy, listed at $61.4 million for 2026 and $86.1 million in 2029.This is Allen's second major payday in Buffalo. His 2021 extension was worth $258 million and carried a then-record $150 million in guarantees. The 2025 deal lifted that guarantee by $100 million. He will be 34 when the final season begins.Baltimore wanted a new deal done before free agency this spring and did not get one. General manager Eric DeCosta said the Ravens "ran out of time," so they restructured Jackson's contract instead. The move cleared nearly $40 million in 2026 cap space, but it pushed a large chunk of money into 2027.Jackson's cap figure is $34.4 million this season. Next year it jumps to $84.3 million.The Ravens have been through this before. Jackson's 2023 deal ended more than two years of fraught talks, and he reportedly wanted a fully guaranteed contract like the $230 million Deshaun Watson received from Cleveland. Baltimore balked at going that far.The Ravens kept pushing into the season. NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported they were still after an agreement before the opener against the Colts. By mid-September, ESPN's Adam Schefter said an extension was likely on hold until 2027. That makes 2026 part of the negotiation. A strong year raises Jackson's price, and he turns 30 in January.Jackson also holds a full no-trade clause, which limits what Baltimore can do if talks stall.Buffalo is in a different spot. With Allen signed through 2030, the Bills know what their quarterback costs for the next four seasons after this one. Baltimore can say that only through 2027, and that final year carries the biggest cap number.
Article Summary: Josh Allen's contract is the newer and larger of the two. Allen signed in March 2025, Jackson in April 2023. Allen's guarantee alone beats Jackson's by $65 million. Baltimore wanted a new deal done before free agency this spring and did not get one.

Article Title: "Couldn't have envisioned this in our wildest dreams": Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes share heartwarming moment with young Chiefs fan after her two open-heart surgeries

Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce give Myka Eilers a day she will never forget

Myka's mother shares emotional reaction to Chiefs stars' surprise

For Myka Eilers, meeting Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce was about much more than getting close to her favorite Kansas City Chiefs stars. The young football fan had spent much of her early life dealing with a serious heart condition. In May 2022, however, she got a day she had always dreamed of when the Chiefs welcomed her to Arrowhead Stadium through the Make-A-Wish Foundation.What followed was a memorable afternoon filled with football, jokes and a few surprises. Mahomes and Kelce took time to play with Myka, who had her own ambitions of reaching the NFL one day. Her mother, Angela Eilers, later struggled to find words for what the experience meant to their family.Myka's journey had not been easy. She was diagnosed with pulmonary valve stenosis as a newborn, a condition that affects blood flow from the heart to the lungs. She underwent two open-heart surgeries as an infant. Doctors also warned that she might need another procedure in the future.Still, Myka refused to let her condition define her childhood. She played soccer, softball and football, eventually becoming the quarterback of her flag football team.She also had a big ambition: becoming the first woman to play in the NFL.Her love for the Chiefs led her to make a special wish through Make-A-Wish. She initially wanted to go on a Disney cruise, but the pandemic delayed those plans. She then changed her wish and asked to meet Mahomes.The surprise arrived in 2022 when KC Wolf, the Chiefs' mascot, showed up at the Eilers family's home in Yorba Linda, California, with an invitation to Kansas City.On May 25, 2022, Myka and her family arrived at Arrowhead Stadium. During the visit, she found a personalized Chiefs jersey with her name and Mahomes' No. 15 in the quarterback's locker.The biggest surprise came when she stepped onto the field and met Mahomes and Kelce. Mahomes welcomed her with a fist bump before joking about his place on the team."Don't take my spot, though," the quarterback told Myka as she prepared to throw a pass to Kelce. He added, "You can't throw it too good, you know."Myka took her shot anyway. She delivered a pass straight to Kelce, who encouraged her with a playful, "Downtown, Charlie Brown. We're going deep, alright?"The Chiefs tight end then joined her for more football, turning the meeting into something far more personal than a quick photograph with two NFL stars.The visit also gave Myka a chance to spend time with Mahomes away from the field. She watched game footage with him, including the quarterback's game-winning touchdown pass to Kelce against the Buffalo Bills in the 2021 AFC Divisional Round.She even signed a one-day contract with the Kansas City Chiefs alongside general manager Brett Veach. It was another special touch for a young fan who had dreamed of being part of the team.Angela later recalled the meeting in an interview with TODAY.com, describing Kelce as "a jokester and a fun guy."She also spoke about what the entire experience meant to her daughter and the family. Speaking to Make-A-Wish, Angela said, "Today has been amazing. It's made her feel so special. Our family just feels welcome and seen. We couldn't have envisioned this in our wildest dreams."Myka also remembered the players warmly, telling TODAY.com that Mahomes and Kelce were "really nice and funny; just good people."For a young girl who had faced two open-heart surgeries before she could even understand the game she loved, the day offered something she could carry with her long after leaving Arrowhead Stadium. Mahomes and Kelce did more than meet a young Chiefs supporter. They gave her the chance to step onto the field, throw passes with her heroes and feel like part of the team.
Article Summary: Myka Eilers was diagnosed with pulmonary valve stenosis as a newborn. She underwent two open-heart surgeries as an infant. Myka wanted to become the first woman to play in the NFL. The Chiefs welcomed her to Arrowhead Stadium through the Make-A-Wish Foundation.

Article Title: "Children with life-threatening allergies": Brittany Mahomes launches $100,000 food allergy campaign after son's health scare

In 2023, Brittany Mahomes found a way to turn one of the scariest moments of her family's life into an effort to protect other children. After her youngest son, Bronze, suffered a frightening allergic reaction to peanuts, the Kansas City Current co-owner decided to support families facing similar challenges. Her personal experience became the driving force behind a fundraising partnership with plant-based nutrition brand OWYN, aimed at supporting food allergy research and helping families deal with potentially life-threatening reactions.The incident happened in August 2023, when Bronze was just eight months old. What began as an ordinary day quickly turned into a medical emergency after the infant experienced an allergic reaction to peanuts. Brittany later shared details of the family's rushed trip to the emergency room on Instagram, describing the experience as “scary and frantic.”For the Mahomes family, the incident was a reminder of how quickly a child's health can become a serious concern. Brittany also called the experience “terrifying,” highlighting the fear parents can face when their children encounter unexpected food allergies.Rather than keeping the experience private, she used it to support an organisation working to make life safer for affected families.On Thursday, December 7, 2023, Brittany and OWYN announced a donation-matching campaign benefiting Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE). The organisation is recognised as the largest private funder of food allergy research in the United States.“I am proud to partner with OWYN on this match donation to FARE. This is a cause that is near and dear to my heart given the support that the nonprofit provides to families like ours who have children with life-threatening food allergies,” Mahomes said.The fundraising partnership formed part of FARE's biggest annual fundraising initiative. Brittany and OWYN pledged to match donations up to $100,000, giving supporters an opportunity to double the impact of their contributions.The campaign also highlighted the challenges faced by households dealing with severe food allergies and sensitivities. OWYN said it wanted to bring greater attention to the issue and encourage more people to support research and affected families.“We are committed to standing with roughly one-third of U.S. households dealing with a severe food allergy or sensitivity, and we’re calling on you to join us,” Mark Olivieri, CEO of OWYN, said. “This medical condition is an undeniable challenge within our food system, and we’re continuing our dedication to tackling it head on with our donation to FARE.”OWYN also became the first brand to receive national recognition from FARE.Donations were accepted through FoodAllergy.org/MahomesOWYN until December 31, 2023. Article Title: 11-year-old Egyptian girl beats 40 million students in reading contest; what Dubai ruler Sheikh Mohammed did after her win caught attention
Article Text:
Photo courtesy: Gulf News

Photo courtesy: Gulf News

Why did Sheikh Mohammed give Mayar his own badge?

Who is Mayar Othman Al Shourbagy, the girl who beat 40 million students?

A competition that brought together over 40 million students

An emotional victory, a Dh500,000 prize and an unexpected gesture from one of the world's most powerful leaders made 11-year-old Mayar Othman Al Shourbagy's moment in Dubai unforgettable. After she was crowned the winner of the 10th Arab Reading Challenge, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum removed the badge he was wearing and pinned it onto the young Egyptian student.Mayar had just achieved something remarkable. She emerged as the champion of the 10th edition of the Arab Reading Challenge, beating more than 40 million students from 60 countries. And as she stood before Sheikh Mohammed, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, he did something that went beyond presenting her with a trophy.According to a report by Gulf News, Sheikh Mohammed kissed Mayar on the head, held her close affectionately and then removed his own badge to pin it onto her.While Sheikh Mohammed did not publicly explain the specific reason behind the gesture, it appeared to be a personal expression of appreciation and encouragement for the young champion. The badge was not part of the announced competition prize. Rather, it was a personal gesture from the Dubai ruler as he congratulated the young student on her achievement.When Mayar’s name was announced as the winner, she jumped up in joy, knelt down and kissed the floor in gratitude before breaking down in tears.This was also not the first time Sheikh Mohammed had gifted his badge to a young student. During a visit to Al Ibda'a Model School in Dubai, he had removed his badge and pinned it onto six-year-old Rayyan Badr Mohammed after the boy confidently recited the ruler's full name, as per Gulf News. That badge was a special-edition Expo 2020 Dubai keepsake.Mayar's victory was the result of a reading journey that began at school. The 11-year-old Egyptian student read 60 books during her preparation for the competition and was selected from among 17,616,289 contestants in Egypt. “My journey began at school, when my supervisor noticed that I could speak Arabic confidently and had an enlightened outlook,” Mayar said according to Gulf News.She initially started reading poetry before moving on to books, summarising them with what she described as wisdom, intelligence and precision. “My mother, father and entire family supported me. My school also provided the right environment that enabled me to win this title,” she said. Her achievement earned her the championship title and a cash prize of Dh500,000.The 10th Arab Reading Challenge attracted 40,286,428 students from 60 countries, representing 138,426 schools and 161,507 supervisors. The initiative, launched by Sheikh Mohammed in 2015, aims to encourage reading, strengthen Arabic language skills and nurture a love for knowledge among younger generations.
Article Summary: Mayar Othman Al Shourbagy, 11, won the 10th edition of the Arab Reading Challenge. She beat more than 40 million students from 60 countries. Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum removed his badge and pinned it onto Mayar.

Article Title: Mahatma Gandhi's grandson 30-acre Virginia land in US reclaimed after 20-month legal battle
Article Text:
Desai said he first visited the Virginia property in 2024 and commissioned a survey at a cost of $4,500.





SURAT: A US court has ordered a Virginia resident to remove his encroachment from land owned by the late Kanu Gandhi, Mahatma Gandhi’s grandson, and his wife Shiva Gandhi, after a 20-month legal battle led by Parimal Desai from Surat.The dispute involved 30 acres of land adjoining Shenandoah National Park in Warren County, Virginia, which the Gandhi couple bought in 1987. During their final years in South Gujarat, they created a charitable trust and transferred their assets to it. Desai now serves as managing trustee.Talking to TOI, Parimal Desai said, “It began when US national Gregory Black sent a legal notice to my residence on Jan 10, 2025. Black claimed the land by the adverse possession rule of Virginia, which allows a person to own land after 15 years of possession if five conditions are met. He ultimately could not prove his exclusive and actual possession condition and the ‘hostile claim’ condition.”Kanu Gandhi and Shiva Gandhi returned to India in 2013 and spent their final years in South Gujarat. Kanu Gandhi died in Surat in Nov 2016. Under his will, his assets passed to Shiva Gandhi.In 2018, Shiva Gandhi established ‘The Dr Schiva and Kanu Ramdas Mohandas Gandhi Charitable Trust’ and registered her will. After her death in 2020, the will was executed and Desai took charge as managing trustee. The trust inherited her properties and financial assets to support its charitable activities.Desai said he first visited the Virginia property in 2024 and commissioned a survey at a cost of $4,500.“As I learnt about the land in Virginia, I went to the property in 2024 and got the survey done. If the trust wanted to do anything with land, it had to be in its possession. I got the will probated in a US court in 2025 and got the land title in the trust’s name,” he said.Black claimed he had occupied the land since 2008. In court he cited trails, a cabin, tree stands, a culvert and other improvements on the property, along with photographs from to support his claim.Desai said, “I had hired lawyers in the US and worked in India to win the claim. I used artificial intelligence (AI) to find the ways to contest the claim. When the final trial took place, from Sep 8 to 11, I told the court that Kanu Gandhi was Mahatma Gandhi’s grandson and he and his wife has donated the properties to the trust, which has the objective of propagating Gandhian philosophy.“We could prove with GIS maps that the cabin was not there for 15 years. I also went there many times since 2020 which disproved his claim of actual possession. We also found another woman residing on the land, which belied Black’s claim that he had exclusive possession.”In the order dated Oct 21, Judge Daryl L. Funk of the Warren County Circuit Court ruled in favour of Desai and the trust. The court directed Black to pay $11,375 towards the fees of the Guardian ad Litem representing unknown heirs.The court also ordered Black to remove the cabin, hunting stands, hunting huts and personal belongings from the property within 30 days at his own expense. Black was directed to surrender possession of the land and cease entering or exercising any ownership rights over it.
Article Summary: Kanu Gandhi and Shiva Gandhi spent their final years in South Gujarat. Kanu Gandhi died in Surat in Nov 2016 and his assets passed to Shiva Gandhi. Shiva Gandhi established ‘The Dr Schiva and Kanu Ramdas Mohandas Gandhi Charitable Trust’ and registered her will in 2020. Parimal Desai took charge as managing trustee.

Article Title: A mother who had to quit her Rs 50 LPA job, now changing chess scene in North India
Article Text:
Nidhi Bhasin Rohilla with her two daughters and prominent chess player Taniya Sachdev (Special Arrangements)

The choice

Shivika Rohilla's first tournament in Delhi U8 State Championship (Special Arrangements)

The pondering

L-R: Shivika Rohilla, her mother Nidhi, and younger sister Rishika (Special Arrangements)

The gap

Shivika's books are used as resources in classes (Special Arrangements)

Listening as strategy

Students take classes at SRCA (Special Arrangements)

What Delhi was missing

From young to old, SRCA has made the game fun for all (Special Arrangements)

The unfinished part

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Have you ever visited a chess tournament? There is a certain kind of silence that persists outside a tournament hall. It belongs to the parents. Behind the doors, children are hunched over boards in a hush so complete you can hear clocks being slapped. Outside, in the corridor, adults sit with water bottles and phones they are not really looking at, waiting for a result that will arrive as a small face in a doorway, either lit or collapsed.Most people spend those hours waiting. Nidhi Bhasin Rohilla was once one among them before she finally huffed, "This is not my cup of tea."Today, the enterprise she has built from the hours of pondering in those noiseless corridors runs events across eight states, more than 40 a month, with about 16 paid staff and roughly 100 volunteers.Nevertheless, it all began with a corporate salesperson who had to choose between her career and her daughter's. Shivika Rohilla , Nidhi's elder daughter, started playing chess in September 2013, aged six and a half. By April next year, she was second at the Delhi State Championship in her age group."We realised that she had achieved this in less than six months of playing chess. That was when we decided to focus more seriously on chess," Nidhi told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction.Nidhi, a dentist by degree, had built a sales career at different top-tier corporate institutions. Her husband, a surgeon, worked at AIIMS Delhi.In 2012-13, Delhi, by her count, had "perhaps only three or four good" chess coaches."We wanted to ensure that Shivika received the right coaching, even if that meant taking her outside Delhi," Shivika's mother shared.With both parents busy earning the fund needed to fuel Shivika’s budding chess career, there was little time for them to travel with her to tournaments."As she started performing well, people recommended that if we wanted her to achieve the required norms and titles, we would need to take her abroad since India did not have enough tournaments of the level required for players pursuing Grandmaster titles," she added. "Initially, I sent my mother with Shivika to participate in these tournaments."The turning point came when Shivika was about 12 and hit a bad stretch. "She was unhappy with her performance and started losing games," Nidhi continued. "Part of the problem was that travelling to South India for coaching regularly was not financially or practically feasible for us. We were managing with the coaching available in Delhi."The coaching was there, but the environment was not. Her school, St. Mary's, had little chess culture, and her friends had mostly quit.Nidhi recalled, "Eventually, she started questioning whether she should continue playing chess. She would ask, 'Why should I continue? What opportunities are there in chess?"At that time, I had to choose between my career and Shivika's chess career. Obviously, when a child has to travel for tournaments, one parent needs to accompany them. That was when I decided I needed to step back from my own career and give her the support she required."Just before the COVID pandemic, Nidhi, who was earning around Rs 50 lakh per annum at that time, left her job for good. "I realised that Shivika needed to travel more frequently. Her rating had reached nearly 2,000, and the next step was to work towards achieving the norms and titles she was pursuing," she recalled."We were spending a tremendous amount of money. We had no external financial support, and everything had to be managed by my husband and me. Our savings were being depleted. Almost everything we earned was going towards chess."The family was getting closer and closer to calling it an end. But a final shot was awaiting as they took Shivika to a top tournament in Brazil, treating it as a verdict."If she performed well and we felt she had a real chance of progressing, we would continue supporting her. Otherwise, we would reconsider our decision," she revealed.Shivika was among the top five in her category. "Her games went well, and people were appreciating her performance," Nidhi said. It was not a full stop after all.Eventually, Shivika's father left salaried work and opened his own hospital."A regular salary is often insufficient to support a serious chess career unless the family has substantial financial resources," Nidhi said. "Some coaches charge Rs 4,000-5,000 per hour."Then came the problem that created the growing chess ecosystem. During Shivika's year off after Class 12, the family paid practice partners Rs 2,000-3,000 an hour."To prepare for games against International Masters and Grandmasters, she needed strong practice opponents who could push her to improve," Nidhi recalled.But, Shivika would mostly beat these practice partners, raising eyebrows of those around her. Therefore, her family felt she was not gaining as much from the sessions as they had hoped.Delhi didn't have enough top-quality players in one place. So Nidhi built one."We wanted to create opportunities for players to meet in cafés and play meaningful practice games," she revealed. There came the Chess Coffee Connect initiative by SR Chess Academy.The idea behind the academy, SRCA, grew from the coaches already working with Shivika. "Since I was already paying for Shivika's coaching, we could use the same arrangement to help other children learn," Nidhi explained.It started with two or three children. Today it has nearly 80."We did not have a website or a formal setup at the beginning. We had a space, a coach, chess books, and Shivika's equipment," Nidhi recalled with a smile.Chess Coffee Connect, the café-based circuit, followed as the answer to the same loneliness that nearly pushed Shivika out of the game.South India, Nidhi feels, has the advantage of community, where players travel together and "analyse their mistakes immediately after playing."Delhi did not have it. "We need to develop a culture in which people continue playing chess and support one another," she added.Now, hundreds of players/chess enthusiasts meet at a particular place almost every week to play games, share ideas, and build a community the north was lacking.Her explanation of the growth that her ventures have seen has little to do with marketing, despite a career spent in it."I work from the heart and maintain a strong connection with the players," she revealed. "Our principle is simple. We listen to what people need and try to provide it."The results read like a list of complaints turned into products. Parents wanted a 25+5 time control for practice before rated events, so she created one. Senior citizens couldn't afford weekly entries, so there is a discount. Mothers said their daughters weren't getting support from their fathers to play, so those girls play free.Through the Helping Hands NGO, some children get free books and classes. Nidhi, however, feels that keeping them in the game is hard: "It can be difficult for them to justify continuing to invest their limited resources."The portfolio has since spread. There are chess-learning cards, including a Grandmaster series she says is trademarked.There is a sports-psychology arm, Mind to Moves, which runs sessions for parents on rating anxiety before major tournaments.There is a Chess Moms Club, born from watching parents guard information about coaches and events.Some of the most telling work isn't aimed at prodigies."We now have senior citizens who come to Chess Coffee Connect and tell us that they played chess in school but have not had an opportunity to play regularly for years," she said, overjoyed. "When they return to the game, it makes everything worthwhile."Besides various theme-based events, the organisation has also hosted a game between a visually impaired player and a sighted one."Chess is a game. It is not only about tournaments, ratings, or winning titles. If a child plays because they genuinely love chess, they may continue enjoying it throughout their lives," she noted.For all the scale, the finances remain stubbornly homemade."Sponsorship is our biggest challenge," she revealed. "We currently have no sponsors, and everything is self-funded."Chess.com's yearly free memberships were the only notable outside help. Federations have been supportive, she feels. But the bigger issue is cost, as she added, "Venues do not provide their facilities for free.""My knowledge of sales, marketing, negotiation, and working with organisations has helped me approach schools and other institutions." But she says she hasn't had to push hard, as invitations came through the front door.Meanwhile, Shivika, now a Woman International Master (WIM), is studying aerospace engineering in London, a five-year course she settled on in Class 7 or 8, and she hasn't stopped playing. She recently won a tournament there.The family has taken the model with her. Chess Coffee Connect has run eight ECF-rated events in England.Asked whether she is satisfied with the work she has managed to do for chess, Nidhi doesn't pretend to be finished. "I could not be happier with what we have accomplished. However, I know there is always more we can do."
Article Summary: Shivika Rohilla started playing chess in September 2013, aged six and a half. By April next year, she was second at the Delhi State Championship in her age group. Delhi, by her count, had "perhaps only three or four good" chess coaches.
