Article Title: 'I wanted to see my career out with Lancs': James Anderson reveals emotional toll of County exit
Article Text:
James Anderson (Photo by Reuters)

Anderson draws parallels between Lancashire and England exits

'Is there something fundamentally wrong with me?': Anderson opens up

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

James Anderson is still coming to terms with an unexpected end to his 25-year association with Lancashire, admitting that the county's decision not to renew his contract has left him questioning his future in cricket. The veteran fast bowler, who had hoped to finish his career at the club he supported as a child, said the experience brought back memories of how his England career came to an end nearly two years ago.The 44-year-old, speaking on the BBC podcast Tailenders, revealed that he has yet to decide whether to find another county or call time on his playing career. Despite the disappointment, Anderson said he was beginning to feel optimistic about the opportunities that lie ahead."I don't know what the end looks like, but obviously I wanted to see my career out with Lancs. I don't know if my career's done, we'll have to wait and see, but it'd be nice, at some point, if someone will let me retire," Anderson said."I'm still sort of trying to process everything, and weigh up what the best way forward for me is, really."Anderson's departure from Lancashire came as a surprise despite his impressive individual performances during the County Championship season.The veteran pacer captained the side and claimed 50 wickets, although Lancashire finished second-last in Division Two.Last month, the club's new director of cricket, Paul Farbrace, informed Anderson that his contract would not be renewed for the 2027 season. Reacting to the development, the fast bowler expressed his disappointment on Instagram, writing that "if it was up to me it wouldn't have ended like this."Anderson revealed that he had initially expected a discussion about Lancashire's performances and the team's plans for the future, rather than a conversation about his own departure."I went in for what I thought was a conversation about how the team moves forward, because obviously it wasn't a great year for the team," he said."Being captain, I thought it was sort of just a chat about that. And then a couple of minutes in, I realised it wasn't a conversation; I was just being told that they thought the best way for the team to move forward is without me. Obviously, I was quite shocked. It was quite brief and, yeah, that was it."The decision brought back memories of his England exit, when the team management informed him nearly two years ago that he was no longer part of their plans.The veteran pacer admitted that Lancashire's decision triggered self-doubt, particularly after he had spent the previous season trying to understand how he could help the team improve.Anderson said he had regularly discussed the team's struggles with the head coach and questioned whether there was anything more he could have done in his role as captain."Last year didn't go too well for us on the field and all the way through the season, myself and the head coach are like, 'Is it something we're doing? Could we be doing more to help the team play better?' I finished the season thinking, 'Was it something I did, but was I doing something wrong?'"And then I get told this news and then I'm thinking that even more. I'm thinking, 'God, this is happening again. Is there something fundamentally wrong with me as a person, as a human being?' But your head just sort of races. I just didn't really know what to make of it for a good week. You're thinking, 'God, I'm never going to play cricket again.' All these sorts of things."Anderson also made it clear that his emotional connection with Lancashire would remain unchanged despite the circumstances of his departure."I am sad the way it ended with the club I supported as a kid but now I have thought about it I am quite excited for the future. I am always going to support Lancashire."
Article Summary: Lancashire have decided not to renew James Anderson's contract. The fast bowler had hoped to finish his career at the club he supported as a child. The 44-year- old has yet to decide whether to find another county or call time on his playing career.

Article Title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' $325 million KC Current opens new doors for 120 children with free soccer league
Article Text:
Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes (Instagram)

Kansas City Current opens doors with its no-cost youth soccer league

Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ KC Current connection to community growth

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In July, the Kansas City Current took a major step towards making soccer more accessible to young players by launching a free youth league in Kansas City’s historic Northeast neighborhood. The initiative aims to remove financial barriers that often prevent children from joining organized sports, while giving them a chance to develop their skills and pursue their dreams. With free uniforms, cleats and equipment, the program offers more than a place to play. It creates an opportunity for families to connect, young athletes to grow and local communities to build a lasting relationship with the game.The league began on July 11 at the 9th and Van Brunt Athletic Fields Park, bringing together around 120 children aged 8 to 10 across eight teams. Players from organizations such as Estrella De Oro, Guadalupe Centers and Mattie Rhodes Center received uniforms, shin guards and Nike cleats without paying a fee.The initiative, presented by CVS Health, aims to increase youth soccer participation, particularly among girls. It also offers support for coaches and referees, helping build a stronger foundation for the sport in the area.Kansas City Mayor Quinton Lucas, Missouri Senator Barbara Washington, Kansas City Current co-founders Angie and Chris Long, and National Women’s Soccer League commissioner Jessica Berman attended the launch.The Current selected the Northeast after consulting local youth soccer organizations about where free playing opportunities were needed most. The area’s recently renovated turf fields also offered a practical home for the program.For families, the savings can make a real difference. Daniel Hernandez, whose nine-year-old daughter Ruby plays for Ryogoku Academy, described the financial pressure of finding an affordable team.“Everything’s expensive,” Hernandez told The Star. “It was pretty hard to find a team like this because her last team, it was 20 bucks here, 20 bucks there, 40 bucks over here, $60 for a uniform. So this is a huge difference, actually.”The Kansas City Current is owned by Angie and Chris Long, along with co-owners including Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes. The club’s community-focused initiative reflects how professional soccer organizations can help create opportunities beyond the field.The program also plans to pay stipends to coaches, who often volunteer their time, and offer teenagers aged 14 and older a pathway to become certified referees. This could give local teens an early chance to earn money while gaining valuable experience.Nine-year-old Margarita Lopez of Estrella De Oro captured the importance of the opportunity during the opening ceremony.“Before, it wasn’t always easy to find a place to play,” Lopez said in her speech. “But now, I can come here with my friends and family and do what I love most.”The league runs through August 29. Its wider goal is to connect families with additional community resources and help more children discover soccer without worrying about the cost. By investing in young players today, the Kansas City Current is working to build a more inclusive future for the sport.
Article Summary: The Kansas City Current has launched a free youth soccer league in Kansas City's historic Northeast neighborhood. The initiative aims to remove financial barriers that often prevent children from joining organized sports. It also offers support for coaches and referees, helping build a stronger foundation for the sport in the area.

Article Title: Nemesis No. 1! Mitchell Santner scripts history, enters record books against India
Article Text:
New Zealand's Mitchell Santner (AP)

Most T20I wickets vs India

31 Mitchell Santner

30 Ish Sodhi

24 Chris Jordan

22 Jofra Archer/Adil Rashid

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner etched his name in the record books during the fourth T20I against India in Auckland on Friday, becoming the leading wicket-taker against India in the shortest format.Santner achieved the landmark after dismissing Nitish Kumar Reddy, taking his tally to 32 wickets in 31 T20Is against India. He surpassed compatriot Ish Sodhi, who has claimed 30 wickets, to move to the top of the list.Santner's latest scalp also marked another milestone in his T20I career as he became only the third New Zealand player to reach 150 wickets in the format. He now has 151 wickets from 142 matches at an average of 23.09, including four four-wicket hauls and best figures of 4/11.Mitchell Santner's tally against India includes two four-wicket hauls, with his best figures being 4/11. Australia's Chris Jordan follows with 24 wickets, while England's Jofra Archer and Adil Rashid have 22 wickets each.Santner returned figures of 2/24 in the fourth T20I, also dismissing Axar Patel, as New Zealand registered their first victory of the five-match series with an emphatic 87-run win. His nine wickets in the ongoing series have come at an average of 11.22. Glenn Phillips ' blistering 107 off 49 balls and Michael Bracewell 's 65 off 25 powered New Zealand to 259/7, the highest T20I total against India. Jacob Duffy then claimed four wickets as India were restricted to 172/9, leaving the visitors with a 3-1 series lead ahead of the final match.
Article Summary: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner becomes leading wicket-taker against India. Santner takes tally to 32 wickets in 31 T20Is against India in shortest format. He surpassed compatriot Ish Sodhi, who has claimed 30 wickets, to move to the top of the list.

Article Title: '1st we lost our land, now compensation': Money from PNB’s Greater Noida branch accounts diverted to 6 accounts in Goa, Mumbai, Jharkhand
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

30 complaints received, many claim gold & silver in locker replaced with faux jewellery

TOI

‘First we lost our land & now our compensation’

TOI





NOIDA: Money allegedly diverted from customers’ accounts at a Punjab National Bank (PNB) branch in Greater Noida reached six bank accounts in Goa, Mumbai and Jharkhand, police have found in their investigation into alleged embezzlement of Rs 35 crore from the branch. Police have frozen the accounts.The police cybercrime team and PNB’s vigilance team, investigating the alleged fraud, said the money didn’t stay in these accounts and have been routed to others. Investigators suspect that branch employees and the bank manager may have come into contact with a cyberfraud gang and allegedly facilitated the irregularities.So far, 30 account holders from Aichhar, Birondi, Bironda, Kyampur and several other neighbouring villages have submitted complaints at Beta 2 police station. The SHO said 12 fresh complaints were filed on Thursday and all the complaints were being clubbed into an FIR filed earlier under BNS Section 316(5) (criminal breach of trust) against the PNB branch staffers.The FIR was lodged on Wednesday after Shrichand, a resident of Viroondi Chakrasenpur village in Surajpur, alleged that Rs 1.16 crore was embezzled from his FD linked to his account at the Aichhar branch.On Thursday, several account holders staged a protest outside the Aichhar branch, with several claiming that gold and silver jewellery and other valuables have gone missing from lockers too.In some cases, these have been replaced with faux ornaments.Some accused bank officials of altering registered mobile numbers and email IDs before diverting money from fixed deposits (FDs) and savings accounts to ensure that account holders did not receive transaction alerts. Many complainants, most of them farmers who had received land compensation from Noida Authority, said their accounts were completely emptied out by the bank staff.Ajipal, a resident of Birondi village, toldthat he received compensation after his family’s land was acquired in 2001 and rented a locker at the bank in 2014. He said he learnt of the alleged fraud on Oct 27 and approached the bank for details on a Rs 35.34 lakh fixed deposit (FD) and 18 tolas (approximately 210 grams) of gold and 1 kg of silver jewellery in his locker, but the bank manager did not give a clear response. He alleged that the mobile number and email ID registered against his account did not match his actual contact details and may have been deliberately changed to stop him from receiving alerts about unauthorised transactions.“On Thursday, bank staffers were asking affected customers to submit affidavits detailing the money held in their fixed deposits (FDs) and the gold and silver jewellery kept in their lockers,” Ajipal said. While the process is meant to document their claims, several account holders said they were still awaiting clear answers about the status of their money and jewellery.Santosh, a resident from Birondi village, alleged that Rs 1.3 crore had been deposited in her bank account as land acquisition compensation, of which Rs 1.2 crore had allegedly gone missing. Expressing anguish over the alleged loss, she said her family had already lost its land to acquisition and had deposited the compensation money in the bank with the expectation that it would secure their future. “First, they took our land, and now the bank has taken away our compensation money,” she said.Meanwhile, senior bank officials from Mumbai and Noida, who have been called in to monitor the case, toldthat audits have been ordered at other branches in Gautam Budh Nagar where land acquisition compensation was deposited over the past two years. Rajesh Bhowmik, the bank’s zonal manager, said a case had been registered with the CBI. Money of three account holders has been credited to their accounts, he said. “…three claims amounting to Rs 43 lakh had been settled as of yesterday (Wednesday). The bank assures its customers that all genuine claims will be honoured,” PNB said in a statement.On Wednesday, PNB suspended the branch manager and four other employees. Bhowmik said the bank will examine each account holder’s case individually before refunding the amounts.“PNB has taken serious cognisance of the complaints regarding alleged financial irregularities involving certain customer fixed/ savings bank deposit accounts at its Greater Noida branch. The matter is being examined on priority, and the bank is extending full cooperation to the authorities concerned and is taking necessary steps to verify the facts, assess the extent of the reported discrepancies and address the concerns of affected customers,” the bank said in a statement.
Article Summary: 30 complaints received, many claim gold & silver in locker replaced with faux jewellery. Money allegedly diverted from customers’ accounts at a Punjab National Bank (PNB) branch in Greater Noida reached six bank accounts in Goa, Mumbai and Jharkhand. Police have frozen the accounts.
